subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening

question: Should OpenClaw permanently support these three opt-in Gateway pre-handshake security controls, including the proposed split between upgrade-time rejection and existing post-handshake origin admission?
rationale: The patch is not merely a bug repair: it adds durable security policy and configuration behavior that can change how reverse-proxy and browser deployments fail when operators opt in.

options.title: Sponsor the opt-in controls
options.body: Keep the default-off design, publish clear proxy/browser prerequisites and recovery guidance, and require final-head wire proof before merge.

options.title: Narrow to one proven control
options.body: Land only the specifically desired pre-upgrade defense and remove the other new configuration settings to avoid an unnecessarily broad Gateway security surface.

options.title: Keep the existing admission boundary
options.body: Decline the new pre-handshake policy surface and retain the current post-handshake origin enforcement while pursuing any approved hardening separately.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the opt-in controls
recommendation.body: Keep the default-off design, publish clear proxy/browser prerequisites and recovery guidance, and require final-head wire proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The available timeline signal points to direct interest in this Gateway security/configuration direction, but repository-history access was unavailable for stronger ownership attribution.
